data.title: Exxon hikes long-term LNG sales forecast on strong demand growth
data.description:
ExxonMobil (XOM) on Monday raised its liquefied natural gas annual sales forecast to reach 50M tons by 2030 - up from an earlier forecast of 40M tons/year - and keep rising beyond the end of the decade, betting on strong long-term demand in Asia and beyond even as the Middle East war causes some countries to rethink their reliance on the fuel.

The company remains bullish about demand growth in the coming decades, citing Asia as a key market for LNG, with 70% of the world's LNG demand by 2050 expected to come from Asia, senior VP for LNG Peter Clarke told Bloomberg in an interview on the sidelines of the Gastech conference in Bangkok.

Clarke said he expects global LNG demand to grow from more than 400M tons today to ~500M tons by 2030, with the U.S. accounting for 30% of the global total, and then double by 2050.

The executive also said Exxon's (XOM) Golden Pass LNG joint venture with QatarEnergy near the Texas-Louisiana border is expected to reach full production toward the end of 2027; the project is expected to export ~18M tons/year of LNG.

Separately, Exxon (XOM) said it took its 264K bbl/day refinery in Joliet, Illinois, offline after ‌a power outage occurred on Sunday.

The Joliet ​refinery supplies gasoline, diesel, and other key fuels to consumers in ​the U.S. Midwest, with capacity to produce ~11M gal/day.

data.title: Aggregate assets under management rise in August
data.description:
Aggregate assets under management at ten major asset managers in the U.S. rose 2.5% from the prior month to $8,458.3B in August.

On a yearly basis, the figure rose by 14.1%.

The benchmark S&P 500 Index (SP500) was up 2.6% to 7,686.4 points in August. Its accompanying State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) saw net outflows of $4.6B during the month.

Technology and retail earnings, a weak July jobs report, in-line inflation data, the Q2 GDP print, a rebound in cryptocurrency prices, and the doubling of the size of bond buybacks by the Treasury shaped broader market returns.

New York-based WisdomTree (WT) posted the biggest month-over-month increase in assets under management during August.

The metric rose to ~$173.7B at the end of August from $163B at the start of the month, having generated $2.1B of net inflows.

Atlanta, Georgia-based Invesco (IVZ) increased its August AUM to $2,562.1B, delivering net long-term inflows of $27.6B. Money market net inflows were $35.8B.

The metric was positively impacted by favorable market returns and foreign exchange.

Victory Capital (VCTR) saw its August-end AUM rise to $356.5B from $345.1B, with client assets increasing to $360.2B from $348.8B.

data.title: Vince Holdings soars as investors start to factor in the OVO deal
data.description:
Vince Holding Corp. (VNHC) showed a gain of over 36% in Monday trading as the bouncy post-earnings action in the apparel stock continued.

Investors may be starting to factor in that the recent OVO deal could be for the company way to evolve from being built around one luxury-apparel label, Vince, into a broader multi-brand retail and licensing platform. The New York City-based company acquired OVO’s operating business last month, including its stores, e-commerce platform, wholesale relationships, operating companies, assets and liabilities in Canada, the U.S., and the United Kingdom.

As part of the transaction, Authentic Brands Group separately acquired the majority of OVO’s intellectual property. Vince paid a nominal amount for the operating business and $6M for a 5% equity interest in the new IP-owning entity, with Authentic owning 51% and rapper Drake owning 44%. Vince (VNCE) also secured an exclusive 10-year license to use the OVO brand IP to manufacture and sell licensed apparel globally, paying royalties to Authentic. That structure is expected to allow Vince (VNCE) to control the commercial execution of OVO without having to purchase majority ownership of the brand itself.

Shares of Vince (VCNE) were up 36.9% at 12:37 p.m. and swapped hands as high as $7.28 earlier in the session. The Seeking Alpha Quant Rating on VNCE has been flashing Strong Buy since April.

data.title: Global yield spike reflects energy shocks, not policy failure - TS Lombard
data.description:
Dario Perkins of TS Lombard is pushing back against media narratives framing the global bond selloff as a crisis of credibility for Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent or Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh.

In the U.S., headlines cast rising yields (US10Y) (US30Y) (US2Y) as a test of Warsh/Bessent credibility; in the U.K., a vote of no-confidence in Burnham; and in the EU, the harbinger of a new euro crisis. Perkins dismissed these as "fun narratives" obscuring a more mundane reality: markets are simply anticipating higher-for-longer energy (USO) (BNO) prices and pricing in a relatively modest mid-course correction in monetary policy, he wrote in a note published Monday.

Perkins said he sparked controversy on social media with a pointed visual response to Bessent's claim that he was "the house" and that bond investors shouldn't bet against him. The reaction was swift and humbling—bond investors immediately bet against him. Perkins's assessment is blunt: "Bessent isn't the house—the Fed is the house. At best, Bessent is one of those servers who plies you with cheap alcohol in the hope that you will keep gambling."

Bond investors remain unimpressed with Bessent's "puny [bond] buyback scheme" and, after 18 months of what Perkins calls "all spin and no delivery," voices calling out the administration's inconsistencies are getting louder—now with air cover from macro hedge fund titan Stanley Druckenmiller, mentor to both Bessent and Warsh.

Perkins finds himself agreeing with Druckenmiller, who reportedly suggested last week he wasn't particularly bothered by the current bond selloff. "Given what's going on in the economy and the capital spending boom and the war for capital, if anything, [bond yields seem] a little low," Druckenmiller had said.

Breaking down U.S. yields into their main components—real expected policy path, inflation expectations and term premia—Perkins noted that real rates (TIP) explain most of the latest move. The rise in real rates is a common global theme, with markets responding largely to the seemingly unresolvable conflict in the Middle East by betting that central banks will raise rates and keep them higher for longer. 

The big moves have come at the two-year horizon, representing a straightforward bet on the policy path. "This is not the work of the bond vigilantes," Perkins wrote. "Nobody is getting punished for losing credibility. Not yet anyway."

data.title: Rheinmetall poised to gain from Germany’s 4th intelligence ship order
data.description:
Germany plans to order a fourth signals intelligence ship as part of its effort to strengthen naval surveillance capabilities, Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said Monday.

The proposed purchase has been included in a draft budget that is being sent to parliament for approval, Pistorius said during a keel-laying ceremony in Wolgast, northeastern Germany. The event marked the start of construction on the third vessel in the new class, which is being built by Rheinmetall.

Pistorius described the ships as essential tools for maintaining awareness of threats in an increasingly unstable security environment. He said they would serve as the navy’s eyes and ears by detecting and analyzing signals and sounds that conventional systems may miss.

Germany’s navy is expected to begin receiving the new class of intelligence-gathering ships in 2029.

A fourth order would expand Rheinmetall’s (RNMBF)(RNMBY) backlog and provide additional long-term revenue visibility in its naval business. The plan also offers another sign that Germany’s defense buildup is extending beyond ammunition and armored vehicles into surveillance, electronic warfare and maritime intelligence. Parliamentary approval is still required, leaving the timing and value of the potential contract uncertain.

data.title: Waymo adds Las Vegas to expanding US robotaxi network
data.description:
Waymo (WAYMO), the autonomous-driving unit of Alphabet (GOOG), began offering paid robotaxi rides in Las Vegas on Monday, expanding its commercial service to a 15th U.S. city.

The company is initially bringing customers into the service gradually, with rides being made available on a rolling basis. Passengers will be transported in Waymo's Ojai minivans.

The Las Vegas launch follows similar phased expansions into Denver, San Diego, and Tampa earlier this month. Amazon-backed Zoox (AMZN) and Hyundai Motor Group-backed Motional (HYMLF) also operate robotaxi services in the Nevada city.

Waymo (WAYMO) has set a goal of reaching 1 million paid rides a week in 20 cities worldwide this year. It currently provides more than 500,000 paid trips each week in the United States and is preparing to test its service in more than a dozen additional markets, including London and Tokyo.

The company said its Las Vegas fleet will initially number in the dozens, with plans to expand it to hundreds. Moove, an Uber-backed (UBER) company that also manages Waymo (WAYMO) vehicles in Phoenix and Miami, will oversee the fleet.

Waymo (WAYMO) has more than 4,000 robotaxis operating in the United States, according to the company.

The vehicles will not initially use Las Vegas freeways. Waymo (WAYMO) said freeway and airport access are typically introduced in later stages of its launches in new cities.

Ahead of the rollout, Waymo (WAYMO) has worked with venues around the Las Vegas Strip to establish designated pickup and drop-off areas. Last month, it reached an agreement with the Las Vegas Raiders and Allegiant Stadium to create a dedicated ride-hailing zone at the venue.

The company said it plans to develop similar arrangements at selected major locations in the future.

data.title: L.A. study sees California facing billions in economic losses if Paramount pulls up stakes
data.description:
A leaked report from the Los Angeles Economic Development Corporation estimates that a Paramount Skydance (PSKY) exit from California could cost the state’s economy billions of dollars if its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) is thwarted.

“Absent a negotiated settlement [with 12 state attorneys general, including California’s Rob Bonta], Paramount has indicated it would be compelled to relocate the company's headquarters and thousands of jobs out of California on October 1 to a more hospitable regulatory environment such as Georgia, Tennessee, or Texas,” the report notes.

To understand the ramifications of such an outcome, the Los Angeles Economic Development Corporation’s (LAEDC) Institute for Applied Economics conducted a preliminary economic and fiscal impact study of the options.

Should Paramount Skydance (PSKY) move its headquarters out of California, the state would experience a loss of 2,750 to 5,550 job-years across all industries and losses between $1.01B and $2.03B in economic output for the 5-year period beginning October 1, 2026.

Once Paramount (PSKY) completes the entire relocation of its headquarters and other operations out of California, the state would experience the permanent loss of ~29K to 58K full-time jobs across all industries and losses between $10.6B and $21.2B annually in economic output.

The study also evaluates the best-case and worst-case scenarios of a Paramount (PSKY) relocation. If the company "slow walks" relocation and reduces spending in California to offset the $1.88B in ticking fees, the commission assumes 30% and 60% of spending reductions would come from operations in California over a five-year period.

The worst-case scenario has Paramount (PSKY) relocating most, if not all, of its operations out of California. This would result in $5.9B to $11.8B (30% to 60% of Paramount’s total operating expenses) being lost.

The LAEDC believes these estimates, while based only on the most recent financial statements and an admittedly fluid situation, are based on conservative assumptions.

“Paramount's departure from the motion picture capital of the world would carry symbolic weight at a time when California’s creative economy is still reeling from 2023’s dual strikes. More importantly, the eventual conversion of its soundstages to commercial or residential use would permanently strip California of production infrastructure that took a century to build and that supports the vendors, crews, and post-production facilities surrounding it,” LAECD said in the report.

Last month, Bonta and Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison scheduled a meeting to hammer out a settlement. However, at the 11th hour, the meeting was canceled amid allegations by Bonta that Paramount (PSKY) leaked confidential and misinterpreted details of earlier discussions between the two.

Bonta shot back that talks are suspended until Paramount (PSKY) “puts a lid on their lying leaks.”

data.title: Excelerate Energy seesaws amid takeover speculation
data.description:
Excelerate Energy (EE) ticked higher by 0.4% and is now down 1% amid some takeover speculation.

A European company is speculated to be one of the bidders interested in Excelerate Energy (EE), according to traders, who cited a Betailve "uncooked alert" that was circulating on Monday. A Western European oil major is said to have approached the company about a deal.

Shares of Excelerate Energy (EE) have jumped 37% this year.

data.title: SpaceXAI, X drop antitrust suit against Apple, keep OpenAI in legal crosshairs
data.description:
The Elon Musk-led SpaceXAI (SPCX) and X filed a motion to dismiss their antitrust lawsuit against Apple (AAPL), according to documents filed Monday in a U.S. District Court in Fort Worth.

SpaceXAI and X filed the suit last year, alleging Apple and OpenAI (OPENAI) were violating antitrust laws by exclusively integrating OpenAI's ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence on the iPhone and other Apple devices.

"Plaintiffs have resolved their claims in this Action against Defendant Apple Inc.," the filing said. "Plaintiffs accordingly move under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41 to dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple. Apple does not oppose this Motion."

The filing does not mention a reason for dismissal or if a settlement has been reached between the parties. 

However, it reads, "For the avoidance of doubt, Plaintiffs do not seek to dismiss any of their claims against Defendants OpenAI Foundation (f/k/a OpenAI, Inc.); OpenAI, L.L.C.; and OpenAI OpCo, LLC."

Apple no longer relies exclusively on OpenAI. In fact, the Cupertino-based tech giant has turned to Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) and is utilizing the Gemini family of large language models to power its AI features.      

"These new capabilities are powered by the next generation of Apple Foundation Models, custom-built in collaboration with Google and its Gemini models for deeply integrated Apple Intelligence experiences," Apple said regarding the latest generation of Apple Intelligence.

data.title: U.S. vs. China: Who takes top AI spot as both nations refuse to slow down?
data.description:
Prediction market odds that a Chinese artificial intelligence model will claim the global top spot this year are curling upward on Kalshi, albeit they remain compressed, amid Beijing's defiant rejection of U.S. calls to slow down AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) development.

Chinese officials on Monday dismissed urgent pleas from U.S. tech executives to pause the deployment of frontier models, labeling the safety warnings as "fearmongering" and characterizing them as part of an outdated "Cold War playbook," NBC News reported.

The pushback coincides with a noticeable shift in prediction markets. The chances of a Chinese AI model ranking number one worldwide this year rose slightly to 14% from around 10% in recent days, according to Kalshi.

The international friction follows a recent proposal spearheaded by Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei—and backed by OpenAI (OPENAI) chief Sam Altman and xAI (X.AI) founder Elon Musk—urging the industry to pace cutting-edge breakthroughs so that security measures and independent expert evaluations can catch up.

However, these industry safety concerns have failed to resonate with political leadership in either nation; President Donald Trump has already rebuffed the tech executives' warnings, stating that the main focus of the U.S. remains firmly on beating China in the global AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) race rather than pumping the brakes.

While U.S. powerhouses OpenAI (OPENAI) (29%), xAI (X.AI) (20%), and Meta (META) (15%) still hold the highest individual odds on Kalshi to produce a top model this year, Chinese contenders are mounting a broad challenge across the field. Entrants like Z.ai (10%) and 01AI (7%) lead a growing pack of Chinese firms in the market, with tech giants Alibaba (BABA), Baidu (BIDU), Moonshot AI, and ByteDance (BDNCE) all trailing close behind.
